subject: Evaluating Replacement Offer vs. Price Match — onboarding & licensing offsets
messages:
From: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acmeco.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procops@acmeco.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluating Replacement Offer vs. Price Match — onboarding & licensing offsets

Hi Kimberly / Sofia,

We received a formal offer from ByteScale (attached) that is materially lower on per-token pricing and includes a 3-month onboarding credit + a dedicated migration SLA. AcmeCo is evaluating whether to pursue a vendor replacement or ask Redwood to match/beat that package.

Key asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a price match on our current consumption profile (Q2 run-rate)?
- If not, can you propose a migration package (one-time onboarding credit, seat/license offsets, or committed-term discount) that closes a ~25–30% delta?
- We need visibility on how a migration would affect our production latency & KV cache behavior — any operational risk notes would be helpful.

Decision window: procurement needs recommendation by July 1. I attached ByteScale's proposal (acmeco_competitor_offer_bytescale.pdf).

Happy to set a short call later today if helpful.

Thanks,
Jane Liu
Sr. Procurement Manager
AcmeCo

Attachment: acmeco_competitor_offer_bytescale.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acmeco.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluating Replacement Offer vs. Price Match — onboarding & licensing offsets

Hi Jane — thanks for the heads up and for sharing the ByteScale offer. We appreciate the candid timeline; we want to keep AcmeCo as a long-term partner.

High-level options we can move quickly on:
1) Price-match + limited onboarding credit: match the competitor unit economics for 6 months on current Q2 profile + a one-time onboarding credit applied to the first invoice.
2) Migration/package offer: a 12-month committed discount (smaller per-unit discount) combined with an onboarding credit and a 30-day SLA uplift for critical routes. This would be structured as a sideletter to your master agreement.

What I need to finalize numbers:
- Confirmed Q2 token/embedding run rates (we can accept your attached file or you can send an export).
- Any committed term preference (6 vs 12 months).
- Whether onboarding credits must be applied to an annual invoice or can be amortized across monthly invoices.

I'll pull together an econ model and a draft sideletter for your review. Can you do a 30-min call tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT? If not, propose a window.

I'll attach a preliminary comparison (redwood_swap_econ_model.xlsx) and a draft sideletter in the next message — want to align internally first.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

(Attachment placeholder: redwood_swap_econ_model.xlsx — internal draft)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Evaluating Replacement Offer — technical notes and license-offset suggestion

Kim / Sofia — quick technical notes to feed into the econ model and the sideletter draft:

1) Runtime/ops considerations:
- ByteScale's stack appears to rely on an inference caching layer that will reduce steady-state token costs for prefix-heavy traffic. Our KV cache characteristics differ (more aggressive prefix reuse across routes). Migration risk: small performance delta expected for specific low-latency routes; we should offer a 30-day rollback clause in the sideletter to mitigate risk.

2) License/offset structure suggestion:
- Offer a one-time licensing offset equal to one month of projected run-rate billed as a credit (can be applied to next invoice or annual invoice depending on procurement).
- If they commit to a 12-month minimum, we propose a graduated discount ladder (month 1–3: 25% off competitor-match pricing, months 4–12: 15% off).

3) Observability & onboarding:
- Propose a hands-on migration window (2-week runbook + priority support) and include a dedicated onboarding SRE for a 60-day window.

I'll attach the model with toggles for amortization period and commitment term (redwood_swap_econ_model.xlsx).

— Jonas
Director, Product Operations (inference)
Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly / Jonas. A few clarifying items before we lock a call: 

- Can you send the econ model with the current Q2 numbers pre-populated? We want to see the precise delta to ByteScale's quoted line items (token vs embedding vs seat).
- The procurement team requires the sideletter to state how credits are applied (invoice-level vs annual reconciliation) and the specific SLA uplift (SLO numbers).
- Does the onboarding SRE entail a shadow period for 7 days where Redwood will co-observe production traffic? If so, we need a short runbook.

Also attaching the ByteScale PDF they sent earlier for reference. If we can get a draft sideletter and the econ model today, we can review ahead of a call tomorrow.

Regards,
